subject: midge larva
title: Dry This Larva to Dust, Wait 17 Years, Add Water. It Wakes Up

scenes.text: This animal can be dried out completely and come back.
The sleeping chironomid, a midge from rock pools in Nigeria and Uganda. Its larva lives in puddles that vanish for months.
As the pool dries, the larva lets its body dry too, down to about 3 percent water. Every process inside it stops.
Dried, it survives minus 270 degrees Celsius, temperatures above boiling, and radiation doses hundreds of times what would kill you.
One larva revived after 17 years in a dry container. Add water, and within about an hour it is wriggling again.
Its trick is a sugar, trehalose, that sets like glass inside its cells and holds everything in place until the rain returns.

description:
The larva of the sleeping chironomid can dry to about 3 percent water, survive for years, and revive when wet.
Polypedilum vanderplanki lives in temporary rock pools in Nigeria and Uganda. In this dried state it tolerates temperatures from near absolute zero to above 100 degrees Celsius and very high radiation doses; one specimen revived after 17 years dry, and rehydrated larvae recover within about an hour. It protects its cells by filling them with the sugar trehalose, which forms a glass-like state. It is the largest animal known to do this.
Which extreme would you least expect any animal to survive?
first_comment: These larvae have been flown to the space station to test how they handle the vacuum and radiation. Which animal would you bet survives space the longest?
